tasks.task: Build a CI pipeline that tests and deploys on push

items.when: When the team deploys by hand and the steps must be captured before anything is automated
When manual build and deploy steps must become a pinned image and a pipeline that tests first
When the pipeline must ship through several environments, such as staging then live
When the pipeline needs keys and you must plan where they are stored, read and rotated
When the build files are written, to find loose permissions and inputs an outsider controls

tasks.task: Write a Dockerfile and Compose set-up for an app

items.when: When it works on one machine only and needs a pinned multi-stage image and local Compose
When only the container files are needed, lean and safe, for an app that already runs
When containers are stopped mid-request and the app must finish live work before exit
When the set-up is written, to run each README step and mark it working or broken

tasks.task: Fix a Docker build or CI run that fails

items.when: When a build fails, or passes on one machine only, and you need the cause and the fixed config
When the failure is inside the app's own tests or scripts and you have the log
When runs break or warn because actions or runtimes are out of support
When the fix depends on a tool's current syntax and you want it checked against its docs

tasks.task: Plan a release with a deploy checklist and rollback

items.when: Before the checklist, for a read-only look at migrations, config and deploy order risks
When one release needs a readiness check, steps with owners and a stop point for each
When the owner wants a short plan: checks, rollback and how to know it worked
When the change should go out in stages with health signals to watch at each one
When risky code should ship switched off, with a kill switch and a removal date
When the team wants a go or no-go, a version and a live check run before every release
When the plan has no answer for a step failing halfway, to design the recovery first

tasks.task: Write release notes from merged changes

items.when: When you have only the commits and need them sorted and the right version bump
When a release is ready and you have the list of merged pull requests or tickets
When customers, engineers and leaders each need the same release told their own way
Before publishing, to catch any line that claims something the release does not do

tasks.task: Check the docs match the new release

items.when: When a change and its release plan are ready and you need test gaps and stale docs found
When one feature changed and you must trace which instructions are now wrong
When docs fall behind every month and need a regular pass
When the set-up steps changed, to prove a new person can still follow them

tasks.task: Write a go-live runbook for a new site or app

items.when: When a first launch needs checks, DNS cutover steps and a watch period after
When domains and redirects must be laid out before the cutover
When the launch includes a big data move and each step needs an owner and a stop point
When the runbook is drafted, to look at the joins between parts and what wins under load
On the day, to get a go or no-go, deploy and proof the new version is being served

tasks.task: Deploy an app to a managed host

items.when: When the host is not chosen, to compare options on cost, security and team fit
When the app suits Vercel and the client wants a live link fast
When the app has workers or a database and Render fits, with a set-up file
After the deploy, so uptime checks and alerts reach a person

tasks.task: Write an environment and server set-up checklist

items.when: When servers exist and you need gaps in alerts, backups and patching found
When each environment needs its own keys and a plan for storing and rotating them
When the set-up needs deploy, maintenance and rollback steps written down

tasks.task: Write or review Terraform for a small cloud set-up

items.when: When a small cloud set-up must be written as modules with safe state
Before anyone applies an infrastructure change, to read the plan for destroys and surprises
When the files are written, to find open buckets and loose access rules
When the change adds AWS permissions and they should grant only what is needed

tasks.task: Add linting, formatting and pre-commit hooks

items.when: When the team has no agreed branch names, commit rules or pull request checklist
When formatting, type and test checks should run before every commit
When the same checks must also run in the pipeline so nothing skips them

tasks.task: Cut slow builds and CI cost

items.when: When the CI bill is high and savings must not remove any check
When you need wasted build minutes, slow jobs and repeated work pointed out
When the fix is layer order and caching in the image build

tasks.task: Keep pipeline secrets and dependencies safe

items.when: When keys sit in the repo or build logs and must be rotated and moved to safe storage
When packages should be checked each week for new flaws and a safe upgrade order
When build workflows may run with more rights than they need

tasks.task: Review a cloud bill and find safe savings

items.when: When you have cost exports and a service list and need top costs, waste and risks ranked
When the client is on AWS and each saving must be weighed against workload risk
When the client is on Azure and needs a resource map, prices and a savings plan
When you can read the AWS account and want idle and unused resources listed with savings
When you want a second view of the savings with reliability checks
When the same waste returns each month, to find the habit that keeps creating it

tasks.task: Run the monthly cloud cost check

items.when: A few days after the bill closes, or when an anomaly or budget alert fires
When cloud and AI bills should be compared each month for what grew and why
When the monthly numbers show a jump that needs a full look

tasks.task: Set up budgets, tags and cost alerts

items.when: After a surprise bill or on a new account, so spend shows by project and alerts reach a person
When code calls paid AI services and needs spending caps and loop limits
When caps are set and someone should check each month that they still fit

tasks.task: Compare the cost of a hosting move

items.when: When two or three hosts are on the table and need a side-by-side with a pick
When the cost depends on traffic and tested limits, not list prices alone
Before comparing, to know what the current set-up really costs and why
When the choice is made, to record why and what was passed over

tasks.task: Review resilience and backups

items.when: When the owner has never said how much data or downtime they can afford to lose
When you check single points of failure, backups and restore tests beside the bill
When a service needs missing timeouts, retries and circuit breakers found
When backups exist but nobody has proved a restore works
When the team is ready to break one part on purpose, safely, to see what happens

tasks.task: Write a blameless incident report after an outage

items.when: When an incident met the client's triggers: downtime, data loss, a rollback or a missed alert
When the cause is still unclear and the possible causes must be checked one by one
When you have chat exports, alerts and deploy logs and need a sourced timeline and actions
When the report must also produce a changed procedure and tracked prevention work
When the report stops at human error, to keep asking why until a process cause appears

tasks.task: Write a customer update about an incident

items.when: When customers were affected and need an honest first notice, progress or final update
When the outage is long and you need every notice plus a record of confirmed facts
When it is over and one short message must own the mistake and say what changes
Before sending, to check promises, facts and tone against what customers complained of
When the draft protects the company first, to start again from the people affected

tasks.task: Write a runbook for the next time it happens

items.when: When someone under pressure must follow the steps without knowing the system well
When the service needs severity levels, first steps and who to tell
When runbooks exist, to find missing owners, stale pages and gaps

tasks.task: Set up monitoring, alerts and reliability targets

items.when: Before adding tools, to choose the metrics, logs and alerts that show real harm
When the team needs targets based on what users feel and alert rules to match
When a small site needs uptime checks, error tracking and a simple on-call plan
When the code itself has no useful logs and they must be added

tasks.task: Review an incident on a cloud service

items.when: When the trouble was on AWS and you need log evidence, a recovery plan and lessons
When you have the time window and need the right log queries and linked deploys
When the findings must become a timeline and report the client can share

tasks.task: Plan a mobile app release

items.when: When an iOS or Android release needs a signing check, a go list and a staged rollout
When the app release depends on a server change that must go first and can roll back

always.when: At the end of any config or code job, to write what changed, why and the proof it works

helpers.when: When a deploy fails because of application code, migrations or an integration
When a release includes a risky migration or a restore must be proven
When the pipeline needs security scans, or an incident looks like a break-in
When the release is an app store submission with builds, labels and review
When release notes or docs need more than a tidy list of changes
When the job is staff accounts, devices or office tools, not the product's servers

gaps: No library item writes two or three differently pitched incident notices to compare before one is sent
No library item writes or fixes GitLab CI or Bitbucket Pipelines files; the CI items are general or GitHub Actions only
No library item diagnoses a failing Docker build or a CI run from its log; only the kit prompt does
No library item reads a Terraform or OpenTofu plan for destroys, replacements and drift
No library item reviews a Google Cloud bill, or a bill from a small host such as DigitalOcean or Hetzner
No library item writes a cost tagging and budget alert plan for AWS, Azure or Google Cloud
No library item prices a hosting move with egress, migration effort and running both for a while
No library item writes a status page entry or sets how often to update customers during an outage
No library item sets up a plain Linux server: users, firewall, reverse proxy, TLS and updates
No library item plans blue-green or canary deploys for a small app without Kubernetes
